trust_decision.summary: Validator._parse_check implicitly trusts a configspec check string to be split into function name and args by a regex with linear cost; _func_re '(.+?)\((.*)\)' backtracks super-linearly on check strings with many '(' and no closing ')'.

landing_point.why: Summary names validate's value/check parsing; _func_re is the first regex applied to the check string in _parse_check, and is commented as 'initial parsing of the checks'.

fix_sites.entry_point: public API Validator.check() / Validator.get_default_value() / ConfigObj.validate(validator) with a configspec; also via `import validate` shim

O3_reason_to_dismiss: Configspecs are developer-authored, not end-user input (the advisory itself says 'exploitable by developer'), so any further regex hardening could be argued unnecessary.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Check strings with nested parens in args must still parse, e.g. keyword=list(...) args and quoted defaults containing '(' or ')'; an over-strict function-name/arg regex breaks them.

O6_input_shapes: check string passed directly to Validator.check
check string from a configspec entry via ConfigObj.validate -> get_default_value/check

O7_producer.where: src/configobj/__init__.py:1933-1950 (_handle_configspec parses the configspec into the strings later passed to the validator at src/configobj/__init__.py:2196 and src/configobj/__init__.py:2203)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: _matchfinder ('^(paramstring)*' with nested lazy alternations) is applied to the same untrusted arg_string right after _func_re and was not touched by the fix; its super-linear behaviour is unverified
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The advisory reproducer targets the function-name split; argument grammar regexes look like a separate concern.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file, ~400 lines away (also applied at src/configobj/validate.py:664)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a value-parsing regex in ConfigObj (_valueexp/_listvalueexp) with a nested quantifier over unquoted values
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: ConfigObj parses config values with hand-written verbose regexes of the same idiom as validate.py; a maintainer extending quoting rules could add an ambiguous alternation.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Restrict the function-name group of _func_re to non-paren characters (or an identifier), which is essentially the published fix.

out_of_scope_notes: src/configobj/__init__.py:1074-1158 holds many other verbose regexes applied to config file content; not this advisory's sink.
